# SHU71 joint host contracts

This correction starts from PR #150 head `f346e539b51ef35a6e4be9f7020bbb5ce6078694`. The two reviewed source files at that head are retained byte-for-byte under `test/fixtures/shu71-history/f346e539b51ef35a6e4be9f7020bbb5ce6078694/` and pinned by `CONTRACT_HISTORICAL_BYTES_PINNED`.

`CONTRACT_PRE_FIX_EVIDENCE_UNSATISFIABLE` evaluates the old gate and production against one filesystem and one custody map. The old gate refuses root-owned evidence, accepts service-owned evidence, and the old production refuses that same service-owned inode. The corrected gate and window both require a non-symlink evidence directory with uid/gid 0:0 and exact mode 0700. The episode directory has the same custody. `/srv/shu/state`, `/srv/shu/state/workspaces`, and `/srv/shu/state/workspaces/supervisor` retain service ownership and exact 0700. Reviewed ancestors remain checked. The joint control also uncovered two additional uses of the contradictory state-parent rule: activation atomic writes and journal ancestry. Their exception is limited to the exact `/srv/shu/state` path and its measured coordinator identity; other journal ancestors remain root-owned.

`CONTRACT_JOINT_PREPARED_HOST` installs the prerequisites into the same backing filesystem and owner map that the production window subsequently uses. All currently applicable rows pass, only the two broker runtime rows defer until service start, and only the drop-in directories/files and activation file defer until arm. The window then reaches ARMED, preserving the service-owned state paths. `CONTRACT_EXACT_GATE_AND_PRODUCTION_PREDICATE` compares both implementations on the same host for root ownership, service ownership, wrong gid, wrong mode, and special mode. Named `CONTRACT_KILL_EXACT_*`, `CONTRACT_KILL_SERVICE_ROOT_ACCEPTANCE`, and `CONTRACT_KILL_STATE_ROOT_ONLY` controls kill changes to those contracts. No remaining contradictory path contract was found.

The account fixture has `shu-coordinator` uid 999 / primary gid 982, `shu-workspace` gid 980 with coordinator membership, and the distinct named group `systemd-journal` at gid 999. Production resolves the local OS system account databases by name, refusing missing, invalid, or aliased primary identities. Activation installation and its phase-bound read-back use the measured primary gid, with root ownership and mode 0640 unchanged. The read-back additionally runs the read-permission probe through named `setpriv --reuid=shu-coordinator --regid=shu-coordinator --init-groups` before dispatch installation. Git and the gate's checkout probe use that same named invocation, allowing NSS to initialize the account's primary and supplementary groups.

`CONTRACT_PRE_FIX_ACTIVATION_UNREADABLE` executes the retained writer, observes its root:999 0640 file, proves the modeled reader cannot read it, and records the old numeric git invocation with cleared groups. Its historical state-parent layout is explicit so this control isolates the gid defect. `CONTRACT_READER_UID_NE_GID`, `CONTRACT_READBACK_REFUSES_SYSTEMD_JOURNAL`, and `CONTRACT_READER_PROBE_REFUSAL` require the corrected file to be readable, reject the wrong group, and preserve refusal before dispatch/restart. Named killing mutants restore uid-as-gid at installation/read-back or omit the reader probe.

`CONTRACT_GIT_SHARED_GROUP_OPERATION` interprets the exact production setpriv argv against the modeled account database and POSIX permissions, including ancestor traversal. `/srv/shu/worktrees` is 999:980 3770; its worker-owned shared child requires group 980. Authorized commands execute real Git object writes in the disposable child. The old invocation cannot access that child; mutants restoring either the old numeric identity or cleared supplementary groups die at `GIT_SHARED_GROUP_ARMED`. Checking only the coordinator-owned top-level directory would not detect the missing supplementary group. The gate checkout control likewise requires a shared-group child and kills `--clear-groups`.

These are executable filesystem/account models with real Git object writes, not kernel execution as the target host accounts. The CI-like harness deliberately removes those accounts and runs as UID 1000. Production's reader probe performs the real named-identity kernel access check when the window runs; this validation does not claim a live target-host operation.

Existing phase-readback ordering, resume remeasurement, D1, runtime deferrals, OS system-account allocation, env-chain custody, named broker/shared-group rules, and prior test assertions remain in place. Historical differential fixtures explicitly retain historical root-owned state; current journal fixtures supply the measured service identity. The documentation changes in older reports only repair source-line anchors. Inventories are additive, and PERMITTED_SKIPS and its entire source file remain byte-identical to the starting head.

Validation uses `test/fixture/shu71-ci-like.sh` with UID 1000, umask 0022, target accounts/runtime/reviewer absent. The focused selection is the previous phase-readback selection plus `shu71-host-contract.test.mjs`; full selection is both coordinator and service `*.test.mjs` globs. Clock runs set `SHU_TEST_CLOCK_OFFSET_MS=31536000000` and import `test/fixture/shift-wall-clock.mjs`. A detached committed snapshot permits the existing committed-inventory guard to exercise the added rows before the new lane commit.

Both full reporters pass the unchanged `evaluateSuite` and exact inventory-name checks; plain and clock outcome streams are byte-identical. The 30 new tests include 14 named killing mutants.

The first full run recorded 3,144 tests, 3,127 passes, nine failures and eight skips. These identified three identity fixture/mutation-anchor issues, two composition counts needing separate accounting for the added reader probe, three historical fixtures needing their original root-owned state, and the recursive inventory failure. The targeted correction suites passed 43 and 32 tests, and the trust suite passed all 872. Existing assertions were preserved; the composition control still requires the prior 132 operations and separately asserts the one new reader probe.

Compressed complete TAP and full reporter streams are stored alongside it, including the initial full failure. Focused clock and both final full runs use the latter snapshot. The final lane commit adds only this completion text and validation artifacts beyond that snapshot; production, test, and inventory bytes are verified identical to it.

PERMITTED_SKIPS, including its trailing newline, is byte-identical to `f346e539b51ef35a6e4be9f7020bbb5ce6078694`: 1,093 bytes, SHA-256 `03cf773e89a89a408d84b707895cae5457cb71094bcc3ba1fe18ad9b9eb2e11e`.
